news.title: Sunderland vs Chelsea: Key statistics and facts
news.body_en: Chelsea head to Sunderland on Sunday looking to make it back-to-back victories in the Premier League. Here are all the key facts and figures you need ahead of kick-off. Chelsea’s win against Manchester United on matchweek nine moved us into the top four in the Premier League table. Sunday’s opponents Sunderland are bottom, with one win and two draws so far. This fixture has seen 124 goals scored in 34 Premier League matches, averaging 3.65 goals per game. Our last victory at the Stadium of Light came in December 2016, when a goal from Cesc Fabregas just before half-time earned us a 1-0 win. We have played there only once since. In the home match in 2016/17, Chelsea won 5-1. Last season’s defeat on the last day of the season was only our second in 14 Premier League visits to the Stadium of Light, where we have recorded 10 wins and two draws. Chelsea are aiming to prevent the Black Cats recording a third consecutive league victory against us for the first time since a run of three between 1999 and 2001. In nine matches we have scored 19 goals (the league average is 12.2) at an average of 2.1 per match. The Blues have recorded the most shots on target in the Premier League this season (53), but faced the second most (50). Chelsea have scored nine Premier League goals in the first five minutes of either half this season. No other team has more than three. The Blues have exceeded that tally only in 2008/09 (10) and 2024/25 (11). Last week against Manchester United, Chelsea achieved our first clean sheet at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League since beating Brentford 2-0 in January. With an average age of 23 years and 89 days, Chelsea named our joint-second youngest starting line-up in a Premier League match (also 23 years and 89 days against Newcastle United in October 2024). Only against Crystal Palace in December 2023 have we had a younger one (23 years and 21 days). On 18 April 1931, at Sunderland’s Roker Park, Chelsea fielded our oldest-ever starting XI, averaging 31 years and 336 days, in a 2-0 defeat with David Calderhead as manager. Morgan Rogers has become the first Chelsea player and second Premier League player to reach 10 goal involvements in all competitions this season (six goals, four assists), after Erling Haaland (13). Chelsea had 39 touches in Man Utd’s box last week, more than we have managed in any other Premier League match this season. Only Frank Lampard (41 from 48) has scored more Premier League penalties for Chelsea than Cole Palmer (19 from 21). Jorginho also scored 19 from his 22 attempts. Romeo Lavia won possession 14 times against Manchester United, the most by a Chelsea player in a Premier League game since Lewis Hall against Fulham in January 2023 (also 14). Carlo Cudicini interview: Sunderland saves, penalty record and personal honour
news.body_en: With the 25th anniversary of a legendary performance from Carlo Cudicini away to Sunderland approaching, we caught up with the former Chelsea goalkeeper ahead of this weekend's visit to Wearside... Earlier this year, Carlo Cudicini was asked a simple question that was far from easy to answer. ‘What was your best performance in a Chelsea shirt?’ The passage of time dictates that memories fade, but those that linger burn the brightest. You could almost see Cudicini whirring through his 200-plus games for the Blues, from his debut in August 1999 to his final appearance for us nearly ten years later. Eventually, he settled on a ‘game at Sunderland, a goalless draw’. For a man who represented Chelsea with such distinction – in high-profile Premier League games, FA Cup finals, Champions League classics – a 0-0 at the Stadium of Light on a wintry December afternoon might be considered an inauspicious response. Watch back the highlights, though, and you get the sense of a goalkeeper at the very top of his game. Kevin Phillips, one of the Premier League’s top strikers at the turn of the century, is denied on three occasions, including from the penalty spot followed by an improbable save with the Italian’s feet from a few yards out. ‘It was probably related more to feeling than anything else,’ Cudicini, now Chelsea’s head of talent and pathways, tells us at Cobham this week when we enquire about that Sunderland performance. ‘Most of the time, a player or a keeper’s performance is just judged on whether he scores or saves, but I think it’s more related to what the feeling was during the game. And that day, there was just no way they were scoring a goal. ‘That was the feeling I probably developed throughout the game, after making the first save. It’s all about momentum. And as well I loved to play away, because you get the feeling the opponents keep coming, you keep saving, and the supporters get frustrated because it’s like going up against a wall.’ Cudicini can recall only a handful of occasions throughout his career when he felt truly unbeatable. The Sunderland game 25 years ago was one of them, and an important factor behind Cudicini’s inner belief that he would not concede was the way he got in Phillips’ head. ‘A big part of being a goalkeeper is the psychological battle with the striker, without a doubt,’ Cudicini explains. ‘If on one side you feel unbeatable, on the other you frustrate the striker who can only say: “What do I have to do?” ‘That gets in their mind. They can overthink it and there’s a component in there saying: “Maybe I’m trying too hard to score.”’ Cudicini remembers a sense of personal pride and satisfaction with his performance at the Stadium of Light, but in the context of the season, it was two points dropped. Claudio Ranieri’s Blues had aspirations of finishing in the top four. Unfortunately, inconsistency continued to plague us. A week prior to the Sunderland game, we took the champions Manchester United apart at Old Trafford, a clinic of counter-attacking football securing a famous 3-0 success. But that was followed by a 1-0 loss at home to lowly Charlton, and then the goalless draw on Wearside. The next weekend, we thrashed top-of-the-table Liverpool 4-0. Cudicini saved yet another penalty in that game, this time from Gary McAllister. His stop from Darren Bent’s spot-kick the following April means he is a member of an exclusive club to have saved a record three penalties in a single Premier League season. ‘Obviously you need a bit of luck, but there were probably two main points to my penalty record,’ reflects Cudicini, who would deny Ruud van Nistelrooy and Thierry Henry from 12 yards later in his Chelsea career. ‘One was my characteristics as a goalkeeper. Not being the tallest meant I was very elastic, very springy, very reactive, and with penalties you need that, because a centimetre can be the difference. ‘At the same time, I did a lot of research at a time when we didn’t have data, like a goalkeeper coach coming in the day before the match saying, “Those are where he took the last ten penalties”. I played at the wrong time for that! ‘I started the work during pre-season, watching every friendly where a lot of times it finished with penalties. I would take notes. Then, during the season, I would watch every episode of Match of the Day, looking at the penalties, what minute they were in, the scoreline, where it was going. ‘So I was going into games having my philosophy around that, based on research I had done, and that year it worked brilliantly.’ The 2001/02 campaign culminated with Cudicini becoming just the fourth goalkeeper to win the Chelsea Player of the Season award. That was no mean feat, partly because Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink and Eidur Gudjohnsen formed a deadly strike partnership that year, scoring a remarkable 52 goals between them. Not only that, but Cudicini didn’t actually establish himself in the Chelsea starting XI until two weeks before the draw at Sunderland. A pre-season injury handed Ed de Goey a place back between the posts on the opening day, and then when the Dutchman’s form dipped, Ranieri turned to Mark Bosnich. It wasn’t until he tore a thigh muscle late on in a goalless draw at Goodison Park that Cudicini was handed his chance. It was one he grabbed with both hands, registering six clean sheets in his first seven games back, not least because of that pair of penalty saves in consecutive weeks. ‘I was disappointed because I thought I’d done enough the season before to start again when I was fit. Mark had a couple of good games, so I understood that, but I was disappointed. ‘I was training very well and thinking that surely it had to change. As a goalkeeper, you either play or you don’t. You can’t come on for 20 minutes. But when Mark got injured, I stepped in. That’s how it works for goalkeepers. ‘I remember I had such huge energy after the Everton game. I came on for Mark and made a good save right at the end to keep it 0-0. All that frustration at not playing built up, and then that good energy and good feeling from the game brought me momentum.’ Cudicini’s presence between the posts proved pivotal in the Blues securing a sixth-placed finish and with it, European football for the following campaign. We did well in the domestic cups, too, reaching the semi-finals of the League Cup and then the final of the FA Cup. Alas, our north London rivals put paid to our hopes of silverware, but our No.23 did still end the season with a trophy in his hands. ‘The Player of the Year didn’t exist at that time in Italy,’ Cudicini says. ‘I remember my first year when I joined Chelsea, and there was the Player of the Year, and I was asking Roberto [Di Matteo], Gianfranco [Zola], obviously Italian guys: "What is this all about?” ‘They explained to me, so I understood its importance. So when I was awarded one, it was a great honour. I was really proud of the relationship that I managed to build with the fans. ‘Personally, that season was probably the most important in my career at Chelsea,' adds Cudicini. 'Coming from Castel di Sangro for £150,000, being alone, not playing at the start, it was all the build-up to that season. ‘A lot of it was down to my relationship with the fans, I think. Coming from Italy, you're passionate, so you get agitated, you get upset, you celebrate with the fans. That was the bond we had.’ As much as memories fade, the image of Cudicini clenching his fists and roaring with joy after saving a penalty will live in Chelsea supporters’ minds for a long while yet.

news.title: Melvine Malard on why there's even more to come from her at Chelsea
news.body_en: Melvine Malard has hit the ground running at Chelsea. Our new number nine has scored eight goals in seven starts and three substitute appearances since signing from Manchester United this summer. Little wonder, then, she is our top scorer so far. Last season, she netted six times in 21 league outings for the Red Devils, but she has now equalled that tally in her first six WSL games with Chelsea. When we sit down with the France international, we mention how her strike rate has so clearly improved. We then ask her what she attributes her good form to, but her answer comes as a surprise. Six goals in six league games, and Malard feels we haven't seen anything yet. ‘I don’t think I’m in my good form yet; that’s the thing,’ she says with a huge smile. ‘Not yet. ‘When you play with a lot of quality individuals, it can help you a lot. Having a positive vibe in your head can also help you a lot. I just need to keep going to reach my top form. ‘What I understand more now with the number nine role is you need to have a lot of patience, and you need to be ready in the box when players give you the ball.’ Malard has settled in so quickly to life at Chelsea. She talks about positivity, and she certainly brings the vibes around the training ground and on the pitch. The time has flown since her arrival in July, and she gives us some insight into the team’s hectic schedule and how she stays focused on the task in front of her. ‘It’s busy, very busy,’ she explains. ‘We play a lot of games with big intensity against a lot of quality players, so it’s busy but very good. ‘When you play well, you feel good, and you win. Also, you score goals. That's my job. I’m very happy to be here and to be doing my job at the moment. I’m taking it game by game. We have a lot of matches, with the Champions League and the national team and everything like that. ‘My job is to help the team when I can: to take responsibility, and take the opportunities I have in front of goal and don’t overthink things. If you make sure you play with passion, you enjoy your football and score the goals. ‘You can see that many people can score in this team, so I don’t worry about it. With good team-mates around you, you know you can have a lot of opportunities, a lot of action in front of goal and okay, if you miss that one, the next player will give you another ball to try again.’ Malard played for Sonia Bompastor from the age of 14. After making the move from her home on the island of La Reunion in the Indian Ocean to play for Lyon, she is now in her second spell under Bompastor and details how the head coach has evolved since then. ‘Sonia is the same,’ she says. ‘The same coach demanding a lot. She’s very exigent with you and your quality. But it’s good to have a coach that pushes you a lot and makes sure you don’t become complacent. ‘She’s maybe a little bit more relaxed here. She shows more happiness. We know in England it’s very free, so she can speak her mind. It’s good to feel free.’ This Saturday sees Chelsea host Everton at Stamford Bridge in the WSL. When we ask her what we can expect, the striker pauses and gives us a thoughtful answer on what a fast start could mean for her team-mates. It’s evident she cares very much about the collective. ‘Everton also have good players, good quality,’ she says when asked about the opposition. ‘They play direct, and when they have the opportunity to shoot, they are not scared to do it, no matter who is in front of them. 'We need to make sure we are always focused on every ball and every player. We want to score quickly. We saw against Charlton that when we score quickly in the first half, we can also allow other players to enjoy the game, like Giulia (Dragoni). 'When she scored her first, she had a lot of emotion because the team did their jobs in the first half and gave her the chance to show her football. If we can do that in every game, it's good for our team, and everyone is happy.' Malard isn’t the kind of player who wants to talk at length about individual accolades. When we ask her about attending last month’s Ballon d’Or ceremony, she once again relates being ranked 28th in the world to how it rewarded the most important people in her life. ‘It was amazing,’ she says. ‘You sacrifice a lot in your life to become a footballer, so it’s special when you are nominated. I went with my wife and my mum. It was a big thank you very much for all the help they have given me in my life. ‘But we need to keep going to be nominated again. Because football is not easy. I went to the ceremony, but now it’s done. We need to move on and keep working hard. ‘I’d like to get higher up the list, but there is a lot of talent so the places are tight. You just need to keep doing your best.’ See Melvine and the Blues in action against Everton at Stamford Bridge on Saturday! Tickets are available here...

news.title: October Chelsea Goal of the Month winner revealed!
news.body_en: For the second month in a row, Morgan Rogers has received the Chelsea Goal of the Month award. Since joining the Blues from Aston Villa in the summer, Rogers has now won two of the three Goal of the Month awards available, including the last two in a row. That has come during a brilliant start to his Chelsea career, which has seen him become the first Blues player – and only the second across the entire Premier League – to reach ten goal involvements (six goals, four assists) in all competitions this season. His two award-winning goals showed very different qualities, too. In September, it was for his instinctive volley into the bottom corner from the edge of the box away at Arsenal. This time around, he finished top of the October poll thanks to his opener against Manchester United at Stamford Bridge, taking the ball from Romeo Lavia near the centre-circle and driving forward through the heart of the defence and into the box, before lifting a composed finish over the keeper. It was a tight race for the October Goal of the Month award, though. Jordan Henderson’s first Chelsea goal, swept in against Bournemouth, came second with 34 per cent of the votes, while the midfielder’s free-kick scored later in the same game was a distant third. However, it is Rogers who triumphs for the second month in a row by receiving 39 per cent of supporters’ votes on the Chelsea Official App.

news.title: Help Mike Penders win Premier League Save of the Month
news.body_en: Mike Penders has received a nomination for the October Premier League Save of the Month award. Our Belgian goalkeeper only made his Premier League debut two weeks ago, when he came off the bench to replace the injured Emiliano Martinez in the 2-0 win away at Everton. Vote for Mike Penders to win the October Premier League Save of the Month award He continued between the posts for our remaining two league fixtures in October, keeping his first solo clean sheet in the most recent of those, when we beat Manchester United 2-0 at Stamford Bridge. It was in that game that Penders produced the stunning save which has been nominated for the monthly award. He showed quick reflexes and excellent agility to divert Bryan Mbeumo’s powerful drive onto the crossbar with his fingertips late on, keeping his clean sheet intact. Alongside Penders, the other five goalkeepers on the award shortlist are Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa), Bart Verbruggen (Brighton & Hove Albion), Christian Walton (Ipswich Town), Walter Benitez and Dean Henderson (both Crystal Palace). The winner will be decided by a public poll and you can help Penders to claim the October Premier League Save of the Month award by casting your vote here before the deadline of midday on Monday 9 November. The winning goalkeeper will be revealed at 2pm on Friday 13 November.

Vote Xabi Alonso for Premier League Manager of the Month
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has been included on the shortlist for the Premier League Manager of the Month award for the second time already this season. Our Spanish manager previously made the shortlist in August, following his first few weeks in the Chelsea dugout, and now receives a nomination for October's award. Vote for Xabi Alonso to win Premier League Manager of the Month It follows a strong month for the Blues, during which we won three of our four league games. That started when we returned from the extended international break with a 5-1 thrashing of Bournemouth, before we took that form on the road to secure our first Premier League clean sheet of the campaign in a 2-0 win at Everton. Following a setback against Tottenham Hotspur, Chelsea got straight back to winning ways on the final day of the month, producing an excellent second-half performance to beat Manchester United 2-0 at Stamford Bridge. Alonso is one of six names on the shortlist for the award, facing competition from Mikel Arteta (Arsenal), Roberto De Zerbi (Tottenham), Unai Emery (Aston Villa), Fabian Hurzeler (Brighton & Hove Albion) and Marco Rose (Bournemouth). You can help the Chelsea manager collect the award by casting your vote for the October Premier League Manager of the Month here before the poll closes at midday on Monday 9 November. The winner will be revealed at midday on Friday 13 November.

news.title: Chelsea loan report: Essugo, Murray-Campbell and Samuels-Smith impress
news.body_en: Chelsea's players out on loan continued their development across Europe and the English football pyramid during October, with several making important contributions for their temporary clubs. We take a look at how the Blues' loanees performed during the month, with Dario Essugo, Harrison Murray-Campbell and Ishe Samuels-Smith among those catching the eye. Dario Essugo started each of Strasbourg’s three games in October, deployed in the centre of the Ligue 1 side’s midfield. He scored the opening goal, his first for the club, in Strasbourg’s 2-1 defeat to Nice, while also playing the full 90 minutes against European champions Paris Saint-Germain. Genesis Antwi and Filip Jorgensen continue to provide a strong contribution with both also starting all three games. Samuels-Smith continued his impressive development at Notts County, featuring in five matches across League One and the EFL Trophy. He completed the full 90 minutes in four of those appearances, including the victories over Sheffield Wednesday and Nottingham Forest’s Under-21s, and demonstrated his versatility by featuring at centre-back and on the left of midfield. Murray-Campbell (pictured top) remains an important member of RC Kortrijk’s defence in his first loan spell in senior football. The 20-year-old played in the games against Genk and Standard Liege, with Kortrijk earning a hard-fought point away from home in the latter. October saw Derry make his debut appearance in the UEFA Champions League during the Portuguese side's 2-0 win away to Lens. The winger provided an assist for Sporting Lisbon in their 2-1 victory over Maritimo in the quarter-finals of the Portuguese League Cup. Wilson has been an ever-present for Rochdale this season, with the highlight of his October a clean sheet kept in a battling 1-0 success over Swindon Town at the start of the month. Seventeen-year-old Kavuma-McQueen enjoyed another productive month with Portsmouth, featuring in six Championship fixtures during October. The young winger made his presence felt particularly in the 3-2 victory over Sheffield United, claiming an assist as Pompey secured an important three points. Walsh continues to gain valuable senior experience at Wigan Athletic, featuring in all six of the League One side's October fixtures. He provided an assist in their game against Huddersfield and started both the Latics’ victories during the month, against Reading and Barrow. Emenalo made his senior debut in October as Celtic beat Hearts 7-1. He followed that up by featuring in the draw with Dundee United. Mhueka was also involved in all three Scottish Premiership fixtures. Satpayev returned to action during October following an injury that restricted his involvement in September. The 18-year-old made three appearances for Burnley, taking his total to seven since joining the Championship club on loan. It was an excellent month for Sarr and Real Sociedad. The defender started each of their six fixtures, with four of those won, including three in La Liga. Those victories have seen them rise to fifth in the table. They also picked up their maiden Europa League victory of the campaign, thrashing Lillestrom 6-0 away from home. Having returned from suspension, Disasi started Palace’s Premier League games against Newcastle and Tottenham towards the end of the month. He also played the full 90 minutes in the Eagles’ Europa League fixtures away to Lyon and Besiktas. Badiashile started four matches for Napoli in the heart of defence, including a Champions League defeat at Villarreal and a thrilling 3-3 draw with Roma. Unfortunately, an injury sustained in that game has ruled him out of Napoli’s past two fixtures. Sanchez played twice for Como, starting their Champions League defeat to Feyenoord and 3-1 Serie A victory over Torino. Garnacho saw more involvement for Villa in October, coming off the bench in four games including the Champions League successes at home to Fenerbahce and Viking Stavanger. Harrison has firmly established himself in Wimbledon’s midfield, starting six of their seven appearances in a busy October. He accumulated more than 300 minutes of football in the process. Richards, meanwhile, is currently sidelined through injury. Kiano Dyer continues to feature regularly for Chesterfield in League Two. He made five appearances for the Spireites, who are currently positioned in tenth place. It was a flawless October for Boreham Wood and Curd, who came into the team at the start of the month. He subsequently played each of their five National League games - all of which were won – and kept two clean sheets in the process. They are already 12 points clear at the top of the table. Merrick was in the opposition goal as Boreham Wood won a dramatic game against Hartlepool 4-3 this past weekend. It was the young keeper’s second appearance of the month, following a 2-1 success against Hornchurch. Sands continues to feature regularly between the posts for Dulwich in the Isthmian Premier League, making four appearances as the south London side sit just outside the play-off positions.

news.title: That’s Proper Chels: Chelsea FC and Chelsea Foundation unite Blues family to support those experiencing loneliness
news.body_en:
Chelsea FC and Chelsea Foundation have joined forces for a third consecutive year to support the Blues' local community through the launch of That's Proper Chels. Inspired by classic Christmas shopping channels, the club's 2026 festive campaign sees a cast of familiar faces showcase the gifts, traditions and unmistakable spirit that make Chelsea unique. Underpinning the campaign is a commitment to making a positive difference. A percentage of sales from our festive range will be donated to Chelsea Foundation and its charity partners, helping to fund work that tackles loneliness and social isolation across London and the communities surrounding the club. Since we launched our first festive campaign in 2024, over £280,000 has been granted to organisations tackling homelessness and loneliness in south-west London and Surrey. Funds have come from the sale of festive products in the Stamford Bridge Megastore and online, along with monetary donations from fans, staff and the wider Chelsea community. Supporters have also donated gifts at men’s and women’s matches in the build-up to Christmas, with 3,200 presents given last year alone and distributed to those in need. This year’s campaign is centred around a nostalgic Chelsea TV network, complete with its own shopping segments, special guests and game shows. Designed to recall a time of families gathering around a TV to watch together, and an era when a shopping catalogue was diligently poured over with pages turned down to mark the much-wanted items, there are appeal messages woven throughout to highlight Christmas is a time for giving. View this post on Instagram            
Players from the men’s and women’s teams lead the campaign, with Ellie Carpenter, Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Alyssa Thompson featuring. The campaign launches today across our social media channels and outdoor advertising spots across the city. There are plenty of winter classics available in the merchandise range on sale online and in store, including three designs of Christmas jumper which, based on previous years, are destined to sell out. As well as two patterns in blue, for 2026 we have a seasonal jersey taking its theme from the famous away shirt that shocked when first unveiled three decades ago, with its unmissable tangerine and graphite colouring. To also help wrap up warm, there are Christmas scarves and hats, while the 2026/27 home, away and third kits make perfect gifts for Blues fans everywhere, as does the selection of stocking-fillers we suggest. Click to see the Chelsea festive range Coming soon and a club-first, Chelsea will bring That's Proper Chels to life with a pop-up retail shop in Covent Garden, London's premier shopping destination, throughout the festive period. The store will serve as a home for all things Chelsea, offering supporters a unique Christmas shopping experience in the heart of the capital. Featuring a TV screen-inspired shop window that transports visitors directly into the world of That's Proper Chels, the pop-up will showcase and sell items from our exclusive festive range alongside products featured in the campaign launch. As supporters shop, they will also be helping to make a difference, with a percentage of proceeds from the festive collection donated to Chelsea Foundation and its charity partners to support their work tackling loneliness. Laura Cordingley, CEO Chelsea Foundation, said: ‘Christmas should be a time of connection and togetherness, but we know that for many people in our local community, it can also be a time of loneliness and isolation. At Chelsea Foundation, we believe in the power of our club to bring people together, create a sense of belonging and make a lasting difference to the lives of those around us. ‘Through the That’s Proper Chels festive campaign, profits from the Christmas range will help fund grants that can be awarded to local organisations who are working tirelessly to tackle loneliness, build connections and ensure that people feel supported, not just at Christmas, but throughout the year. ‘Every purchase can help us extend that support to those who need it most. It’s a powerful example of how, together, we can turn pride in our club into positive change in our community.’ In the build-up to Christmas, Chelsea Foundation will host its annual festive lunch at Stamford Bridge, supporting those experiencing loneliness. Supporters will have the opportunity to donate gifts similar to last year at designated drop-off points at all Stamford Bridge matches for both men’s and women's teams, from 14 November. To donate £5 to support those experiencing loneliness this Christmas, please text CFCFOUNDATION to 70085

news.title: UEFA Youth League report: Cobham Next Gen 2-3 Flora Tallinn (4-5 aggregate)
news.body_en: Chelsea Cobham Next Gen exited the UEFA Youth League after a 3-2 defeat to Flora Tallinn. We went ahead within two minutes of both halves but a late penalty sent us out of the competition. Mathis Eboue gave us an early lead with a low, driven finish into the far corner, but Sander Alamaa equalised shortly afterwards, making it 1-1 at half-time. In the second half, we began in similar fashion with Ibrahim Rabbaj putting us back in front with his second touch after coming off the bench. Unfortunately, Flora responded quickly again, this time through Marten Kukkonen. They later took the lead from the penalty spot through Alamaa, ending our European aspirations this term. Flora enjoyed a fast start in the reverse fixture, but today it was Chelsea who set the tone immediately, going ahead within two minutes. Yisa Alao lofted the ball up to Ezenwata who nodded it into the path of Eboue. The Blues winger initially stood up his marker before dropping a shoulder, going down the line and rifling his shot against the post and into the bottom corner. Our lead didn’t last long as Alamaa, who scored a brace in the first leg, pickpocketed Alfie Osborne and went through on goal to equalise. We enjoyed the better chances of the first half and neared our second of the afternoon when Ezenwata played a driven pass across the face of goal. Eboue met it first but miskicked his shot, and the ball subsequently fell to Alao, whose effort was snuffed out by Andero Tatrik. At the interval, the score remained level both on the afternoon and on aggregate. Rabbaj was introduced in the second half, replacing Osborne, and made an instant impact. Eboue proved a threat again down the left wing and cut back towards the penalty spot, where Rabbaj was waiting to tuck home with only his second touch. Unfortunately, Flora got back on level terms eight minutes later through Kukkonen. In the 69th minute, Grimwade picked up the ball on the edge of the box surrounded; he wriggled in and out, dodging at least three Flora defenders, before aiming for the top corner - but his effort sailed just over. Flora Tallinn won a penalty with 12 minutes remaining, which was converted by Alamaa to put the visitors in front. Eboue tried to provide the response, when he cut inside and went for the spectacular, but his strike was off target. Andrew Pennie was played through with limited minutes left on the clock, his shot was hard and low but denied by Flora. There were five minutes of additional time and we pushed for an equaliser, but we couldn’t find the all-important goal. This defeat spells the end of our involvement in this season's UEFA Youth League. Cobham Next Gen visit London rivals Tottenham Hotspur this Sunday at the Lamex Stadium. The game gets underway at 1pm GMT and supporters can watch the match live with a CFC+ subscription. news.title: Veerle Buurman on the Ballon d'Or and playing in front of Hannah Hampton
news.body_en: It’s been another strong start to the season for Veerle Buurman. Still only 20, the defender has started nine of our 13 matches this season and looks as assured as players with many more years of experience. At the end of her first campaign with Chelsea, the Dutch international won the Women’s Super League Rising Star Award for her outstanding performances in the backline during 2025/26. Now that she is used to playing in the WSL, she reflected on the strength of the league and picked out her standout moments from her time with the Blues so far. ‘The quality in the whole league, all the teams, is going up,’ she explained. ‘Every weekend there's a big game, and it’s important to take the three points. There’s never an easy game. ‘This is my second season at Chelsea, and winning the Rising Star Award from the WSL was of course really nice. 'I’d also pick out my first goal for Chelsea as another big moment, but being a part of this team means a lot already, and I’m enjoying my football here, being on the pitch with a lot of girls I can learn from.’ Buurman also attended this year’s Ballon d’Or ceremony, having been named on the five-player shortlist for the Women’s Young Talent of the Year award. Barcelona’s Vicky Lopez scooped the trophy on this occasion, but the youngster reflected on how it felt to be named as one of the five best young talents in world football. ‘It meant a lot to be nominated,’ she said. ‘I never expected it, but I was really proud and happy. A lot of the girls came to me to say congratulations when I found out – it was a really nice moment on the pitch before training.’ It must be reassuring for a young defender to be playing in front of a goalkeeper of Hannah Hampton’s calibre. Buurman took the time to praise her Chelsea colleague and explained why she feels so at ease with her as the last line of defence. ‘Hannah is really good,’ she continued. ‘She's showing it on the field in every game in terms of when she's on the line, but also on the ball. Her passing is amazing, and she's showing every season how good she is on the field. ‘If you're playing and you know Hannah is behind you in goal, that's really nice. You feel confident. You know she has your back. She’s making saves, she also has a lot of confidence on the ball, and she's showing that every game.’ It’s not just at Chelsea that Buurman is thriving. She’s already earned 20 caps for the Netherlands and will be at the Women’s World Cup in 2027 should they come through their qualifying double header against Slovenia in early December. ‘Every time you put on the national team shirt, it's something to be really proud of and never gets normal,’ she concluded. ‘We have important games coming up in the next international window. We need to qualify for the World Cup. If we qualify, it will be amazing to be there as a team.’

Marco Palestra: My Football Firsts
news.body_en: After making his full Chelsea debut at the weekend, Marco Palestra shares his earliest memories and experiences in football. The Italian full-back had to wait to make his first start for the Blues, in Saturday's 2-0 win over Manchester United at Stamford Bridge, following his summer move from Atalanta, and now he answers our quickfire questions so you can get to know him a little better... What was the first football match you went to? The first match that I remember that I went to see was Atalanta against Palermo in Bergamo. Atalanta lost 1-0, I remember, and I had just joined Atalanta. I was 10 years old, I think. What was the first football kit you owned? I think one of my first jerseys that I had was one of Ronaldinho, a Brazil shirt. I remember that one. What was the first team you played for? The first team I played for was Assago, which is near where I was born. I played there for four years, it was a good time. Who was the first coach who gave you important advice? I can’t remember any specific advice but maybe when I was a bit older, like 16, our coach that changed my position. His name is Marco Fioretto. So he was the first one who moved me from midfield to out wide and he maybe changed my career. Who was your first team-mate who became a friend? I have one of my best friends, his name is Filippo Bonvento. I met him when I started playing at Assago when I was about four years old, and now he is still my best friend. So for sure him. Who was your first professional game against? My debut in professional football isn’t good, because I got a red card. I played for Atalanta Under-23s in the third league, Serie C, and I remember it was a difficult game and I got a red card, so it’s maybe not the best debut. I probably deserved it, it was two yellows because I made two fouls, but I didn’t have any experience at the time. Who was your first goal against? I will always remember my first goal. Again, it was for Atalanta Under-23s in the third league. It was against Albinoleffe, who are local rivals in Bergamo. The game finished 1-1, and I scored the first goal with a header. Can you remember the first time somebody recognised you in public? I don’t know. I think it would have been in Bergamo when I started to play in the third league with the Under-23s, probably around the city one guy recognised me. What was your first emotion when you signed for Chelsea? I was just happy because when I was young I never thought I could be a Chelsea player. So the first emotion was only happiness. Now I am still happy, but I need to improve myself to win with this team.

news.title: Romeo Lavia wins Premier League Player of the Matchweek award
news.body_en: Romeo Lavia has been named the Premier League's Player of the Matchweek following his outstanding performance in Chelsea's 2-0 victory over Manchester United at Stamford Bridge The Belgian midfielder produced an excellent all-round display as the Blues returned to winning ways on Saturday, playing an influential role in the heart of midfield and helping Xabi Alonso's side secure all three points. Lavia's composure in possession, ability to break up opposition attacks and intelligent distribution were key to Chelsea's impressive performance, while he also played an important part in our opening goal. It was the 22-year-old who won possession in midfield before supplying the pass for Morgan Rogers to break the deadlock early in the second half, with Cole Palmer later doubling our advantage from the penalty spot. Having already been voted Player of the Match by supporters on the Chelsea Official App, Lavia has now added another individual accolade following a vote by football fans on the Premier League's official website. Our No.45 came out on top in a six-player shortlist that also featured Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Oli McBurnie, Declan Rice, Jan Paul van Hecke and Bart Verbruggen. Speaking after Saturday's victory, Lavia reflected on the hard work behind his performances. He said: 'I feel very comfortable. Like I've always said, it's been in the weeks a lot of work that goes unseen with everyone in the building, at the training ground. So I'm very happy that it's all paying off and hopefully it just continues this way.' Head coach Alonso was also full of praise for the Belgian following his influential display against United. 'It was a top performance. In the last three weeks, I've seen a Romeo in top form. He is feeling good and feeling confident,' said Alonso. 'His game, from a midfielder's point of view, was very complete. He has done so many good things and I'm happy for him. He deserves huge recognition.' And that recognition has now arrived, with Lavia's latest accolade providing another reason to celebrate an impressive individual performance and an important Chelsea victory.

news.title: WNL Cup Report: Oxford United Women 1-1 Chelsea Women Under-18s (3-4 on pens)
news.body_en: Chelsea Women’s Under-18s, who play in the PGA Under-21 Women’s League, reached the second round of the Women’s National League Cup after beating Oxford United Women 4-3 on penalties following a 1-1 draw at the MGroup Stadium. Carla Gardiner (in the picture above) gave the Blues a first-half lead before Oxford levelled shortly before the break. With the score level after 90 minutes, the tie went straight to a shootout, where Victoria Rudz saved Oxford’s fourth penalty and Gabi Storey scored the winning kick. Chelsea competed very well against an Oxford side who are top of the third tier and had not lost in any competition this season. Leanne Champ’s side edged the possession statistics and worked tirelessly throughout. The Blues showed great character and intent to go further in this competition than in previous years. Chelsea went ahead on 27 minutes. Patient combination play around our own box involving Storey, Lola Brown and Keira Johnson ended with the ball returned to Rudz, who went longer into the wide left channel under pressure from an Oxford forward. A mix-up between Oxford’s central midfielder and full-back sent the ball into the air, and Brown capitalised to restart the attack. She drove forward into space with options on either side and picked out Gardiner, who had peeled off to the left. Gardiner took a touch inside the box and unbalanced the Oxford centre-back with quick feet. The defender raised a leg to block, and the shot deflected into the net. Oxford equalised two minutes before half-time. Storey and Chloe Sarwie played short from a Chelsea goal kick to find captain Belle Sullivan centrally, but good Oxford pressure forced the Blues into a mistake, with the Yellows' number 10 slipping her finish across Rudz and into the net. Champ made a double change on the hour, as Aysia Matabaro and Stevie Sinclair replaced Rebekah Pierce and Gardiner. The score remained 1-1 at full-time, and under competition rules the tie went straight to penalties, with Oxford going first. Oxford converted their first three kicks, sending Rudz the wrong way each time. Brown buried Chelsea’s first low into the corner, and Chelsea N’Drin scored straight down the middle, but Sinclair’s effort went just wide of the left post. Rudz read Oxford’s fourth penalty well, saving a slow effort down to her right, and Nelly Las drove low and hard into the corner to level the shootout at 3-3. Oxford’s fifth taker then blasted high over the bar, and Storey stepped up to squeeze a low, hard penalty in past the goalkeeper to send the Blues through. Chelsea are in the draw for the second round of the Women’s National League Cup. The draw takes place at 7pm on Wednesday 4 November and will be shown on the FA WNL YouTube channel. The Blues return to PGA Division 1 action on Wednesday 4 November, when Sunderland travel to Cobham. news.title: Lavia on Hazard: ‘I could see in his eyes he was happy for me’
news.body_en: Not long after the dust had settled on our win over Manchester United on Saturday, a very special guest waited to greet the Chelsea players before they headed home. Eden Hazard was stationed just outside the tunnel at Stamford Bridge having watched his former club triumph courtesy of goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer. Our brilliant former attacker was especially excited to meet Palmer, who now adorns the No.10 shirt with similar skill and verve as Hazard did, but also his compatriots Mike Penders and Romeo Lavia, both of whom had starred in the game. Lavia has enjoyed his start to the campaign, which has included a return to the Belgium national team. He was thrilled to speak to Hazard, a bona fide Chelsea and Red Devils great who he hopes to emulate in time. ‘He’s a very important figure for me,’ said Lavia. ‘We speak quite a lot. It was good to see him out here, and I could see in his eyes he was happy for me and proud. It gives me that extra motivation.’ For Lavia, it has been a season of steady progress. He has been in the matchday squad for every Premier League fixture so far, and last week completed two 90-minute matches in the space of four days. His displays in those games, against Liverpool and Man United, highlighted just what the 22-year-old is capable of. Now he is determined to maintain those levels of performance and his fitness. ‘As long as I feel good, I will do everything possible to help the team get results. I’m feeling good, so I am very happy with my performance. ‘I’m still young and there are a lot of areas I can improve. We try to tick them off during the week. It’s a process. ‘All I can say is the work we are doing with all the people at the club is going well so far. It’s just about keeping it going and hopefully we can continue this way.’ Eden Hazard will be back at the Bridge when Chelsea Legends take on Tottenham on 27 March, with tickets on general sale here now!

Vote for your Chelsea Women's Constant Contact Goal of the Month
news.body_en: It's been a perfect month for Sonia Bompastor and her Chelsea side, with four wins from four in the Women's Super League and Women's Champions League. Now it is time to pick your standout CFCW strike from October! There are plenty of goals to choose from in October, with the Blues netting 14 times across four matches. We started with a 3-0 away win over West Ham United before the international break, and when our players returned from representing their respective nations, we recorded a memorable 6-2 victory over Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge. That was followed by a 3-1 win at Crystal Palace the following weekend, and the month concluded with a 2-0 win against Roma in the Women's Champions League at Plough Lane. Which Chelsea goal in October was your favourite? View the shortlisted strikes above and then submit your vote on the Chelsea Official App, where the winner of the award, presented by Constant Contact, will be revealed in the coming days. Sjoeke Nusken started the move for our first strike of the afternoon in Dagenham, sensing a moment's hesitation from West Ham when they took a free-kick in their own half. The German international stole the ball, strode forward and picked out Malard. The number nine received it with her back to goal, but stood strong, turned and stroked her finish into the bottom corner. Doubling our lead against the Hammers was Walsh. The move began with Alyssa Thompson jinking her way towards goal from the left-hand side before playing a short sideways pass for Wieke Kaptein, who then shifted the ball quickly to Walsh. The experienced midfielder used her tried and tested technique from range to lash the ball into the bottom corner to the delight of the travelling fans. James' second goal in our 6-2 win over Spurs at Stamford Bridge was a solo effort as she sprinted forward on the break to take matters into her own hands for the second time in that match. Breaking free of the backpedalling defenders, she burst into the box on the left and used her low centre of gravity to lean backwards and curl a superb shot into the bottom right-hand corner. While James' goal came courtesy of a delicate touch, second-half substitute Nusken scored with a pile-driver of a shot to give the Spurs 'keeper Lize Kop no chance of making a save. Finding space in the box, the midfielder blasted home with pure conviction, putting us firmly in the driving seat. Hamano came on after half-time against Spurs, and she marked her appearance against her former loan club with a stunning swerving effort from almost 30 yards out. The replays showed just how much the ball moved once it had left her foot, and the goal certainly got the Blues fans off their seats at Stamford Bridge. Known more for her instinctive finishes from inside the penalty area, Malard's second entry on this list came from distance. As the space opened up 25 yards out following a Katie McCabe throw-in, Malard found herself in space and unleashed a stunning strike that fizzed past a helpless Pauline Peyraud-Magnin in the Palace goal. news.title: Chelsea and Linglong Tire bring The Famous CFC back to China
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club and global partner Linglong Tire today announce the latest stop for The Famous CFC. The club, including legendary captain Cesar Azpilicueta, will be in Chengdu, China, from 4-6 December for a special fan event ahead of our Premier League fixture against Liverpool. With support from Linglong Tire, this will be the club’s third visit to China for the Famous CFC, following trips to Shanghai and Chongqing. During those visits, Blues legends Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink and Gianfranco Zola met Chelsea supporters in China, who always give the club a warm welcome. Joining Chelsea FC in Chengdu will be club legend Azpilicueta, who will spend the weekend meeting supporters and sharing stories from his decorated career in blue. news.title: OTD: The Blues run riot in Rome
news.body_en: A new-look Chelsea team announced their European credentials with a 4-0 thrashing of Lazio on this day in 2003. The Blues, with plenty of exciting new players in the side, had started our second Champions League campaign solidly, if unspectacularly. We had bagged a late winner against Sparta in Prague before losing at home to Besiktas. A come-from-behind victory against Lazio followed at Stamford Bridge before the teams reconvened in Rome a fortnight later. Nearly 50,000 people packed inside the Stadio Olimpico, including several thousand travelling Chelsea supporters. They witnessed a masterclass from Claudio Ranieri's side. Hernan Crespo, a serial scorer in Serie A before his move to Chelsea, bundled us ahead on the quarter-hour mark, and our cause was made easier early in the second half when Sinisa Mihajlovic was eventually dismissed. We made our numerical advantage count in style, picking off the Roman side with three goals in ten minutes. Eidur Gudjohnsen, Damien Duff and Frank Lampard were the scorers, sealing a victory that made Europe sit up and take notice. We would eventually reach the semi-finals before being agonisingly knocked out by Monaco. You can watch highlights of the famous Lazio win and the story of a memorable second Champions League campaign below.

news.title: Training gallery: The work starts again at Cobham
Not On Our Pitch: Chelsea FC Women and Flo show period shame the Pink Card
news.body_en: Chelsea FC Women and Here We Flo are back for year two of our partnership with Not On Our Pitch. The campaign calls out the everyday habits period shame teaches us, and shows them the Pink Card. The tampon up the sleeve. The cough to cover a crinkling wrapper. The whispered ‘have you got a spare…you know?’ Period shame teaches menstruators to hide something half the population experiences every month. According to the Youth Sport Trust, periods are the single biggest barrier to sport for teenage girls (up to 52%). Every hidden product or whispered phrase reinforces the stigma. To tackle period shame, Chelsea FC Women and Here We Flo, the period care brand which is CFCW's back of short partner, are launching year two of our partnership with a new campaign, Not On Our Pitch, giving the 'pink card' to period shame in football and beyond. Giulia Mazzia, Chelsea FC Women's Chief Revenue Officer, said: 'As a club, we are committed to using our platform to drive conversations that matter, and tackling period shame is one of them. Through our partnership with Here We Flo, we want to challenge the stigma that still surrounds menstruation, confront uncomfortable truths and encourage more open, honest conversations. 'This partnership goes far beyond visibility on our players' shorts. It reflects how we show up every day as a club, using our voice to help create a future where the next generation no longer carries the burden of period shame. We are grateful to Here We Flo for sharing that ambition and helping us drive meaningful change.' Susan Allen-Augustin, co-founder, Here We Flo, added: ‘Last season, We Don’t Bleed Blue achieved 1.6 billion in global press reach. This year, we’re going further, calling out the behaviours that let period shame thrive, on and off the pitch. With Chelsea FC Women now at home at Stamford Bridge, it is the perfect moment to set new standards for the game and beyond.’ A red card sends a player off the pitch, but a pink card sends off period shame. Behaviours like hiding a tampon up your sleeve, whispering about your period, or replying on euphemisms 'like time of the month' no longer have a place in the game. Here We Flo and Chelsea Women Players will address period shame on social media, stadium screens and matchday programmes, tackling myths alongside gynaecologists. Just as referees send off foul play, players and fans can use the Flo Pink Card to call out period shame habits whenever they spot it.

news.title: Giulia Dragoni: 'I want young Italian girls to dream of playing for Chelsea'
news.body_en: Summer signing Giulia Dragoni couldn't hold back her emotions when her shot hit the back of the net during our 6-0 win over Charlton Athletic at the weekend, and it's no wonder her eyes were filled with tears. Still only 19 and navigating a move away from her home country, the Italian midfielder has fought for minutes this season amid strong competition in her position. Sonia Bompastor has praised her strong mentality and determination to improve, explaining how the youngster continually asks for feedback on her performance. The head coach is confident more playing time will come, and Dragoni did her chances no harm by scoring her first competitive goal for Chelsea after being introduced as a second-half substitute against Charlton. Yet it was matters off the pitch that were on the agenda when we sat down to talk to her, and it appears she's settling well in her new home. 'It’s been really nice since I moved here,' she smiles. 'It's already been three months. I came here, and I didn't know what to expect from my team-mates, to be honest. Of course, I knew Keira (Walsh) and Lucy (Bronze) from Barcelona, but I was really young then; I was a little kid. Now I'm a bit different as a person and a player. 'Everyone, since the first day, has helped me a lot to adapt better to the language, to the training, to a different kind of football. They are trying to make me feel as comfortable as they can, and I'm really enjoying my time here. 'I really enjoyed our tour to Australia and New Zealand; it was a nice first few weeks. Since then, I’ve been learning every day in training and trying to take in everything that I can from the other players. My English is improving, but I think I can get better. 'Of the three languages that I can speak (Italian, Spanish and English), English is the one that I speak the worst. But I'm happy, and I'm watching a lot of series in English to learn better.' Back home in Italy, the spotlight has been on Dragoni's move to Chelsea. There, the women's game is still developing, so to see a young talent make the move to a side with multiple trophies and big ambitions has been a big deal. Dragoni is not the kind of player to let such attention go to her head, and is instead content with the thought she might be making a difference as a role model to aspiring young players back home. 'I like to think about myself as a normal, almost 20-year-old girl,' she continues. 'I'm happy that little girls from Italy are thinking about me as a kind of inspiration, you know? 'I hope that some of these little girls can now dream of being at Chelsea if they really want to one day, and if they keep working hard, nothing is impossible. But I want to keep my feet on the ground. I'm that kind of person.' The teenager is no stranger to living in big cities. Born in Milan, she earned a move to Barcelona in January 2023, before spending two seasons on loan at Roma in Italy's capital. And while she is now enjoying London, her patriotism shines through when asked to compare the UK capital with Rome. 'Rome is really nice. I think it's one of the best cities in the world, to be honest,' she says. 'Once you’ve lived there, it's really hard to compare Rome to other cities. As an Italian, I really love Rome, but I'm enjoying London so far as well, even if the weather is not the best! 'I'm maybe more of a country girl now. I think I’m a bit tired of too many people. We have nice parks and areas where we can walk near the training ground. That's the part I'm enjoying the most: being a bit calmer and having time on my own for a bit.' Saturday's match with Everton at Stamford Bridge coincides with Dragoni's 20th birthday, and she shares her special day with Alyssa Thompson, who will turn 22 on 7 November. The Italian is looking forward to the celebrations for one particular reason. She said: 'It’s good, because I don't want to have all the attention on me, so we can share it!'

news.title: Vote for Chelsea’s October Goal of the Month
news.body_en: There was no shortage of superb Chelsea goals scored in October, and now we want you to choose the best of the bunch. Our shortlist of nine contains goals from our men’s, Cobham Next Gen and Under-18 teams, in what is bound to be a closely contested vote. Make sure you have your say by watching the contenders above and then picking your favourite on the Chelsea Official App, which you can download here! The winner will be revealed on the Chelsea Official App soon! Grimwade whipped a stunning free-kick into the top left-hand corner, the dip and swerve on the ball too hot for the visiting keeper to handle. Henderson opened his Chelsea account a couple of minutes into his home debut in style, bending a wonderful finish into the Shed End net via the inside of the post. Joao Pedro’s first of the afternoon stemmed from good work from Pedro Neto down the right, before the Brazilian instinctively fired home a right-footed finish into the roof of the Bournemouth net. Henderson’s afternoon got even better when he bagged his second of the afternoon, curling a free-kick into the top right-hand corner with Djordje Petrovic helpless to stop it. Strong hold-up play from Morgan Rogers allowed Jorrel Hato to dart down the left flank, beating his man before finding Neto in the middle, who stroked his finish into the net to give us the lead at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. Pennie darted from inside his own half, evading one sliding challenge before running in on goal and calmly finishing on his right. Grimwade’s second nomination is for an almost carbon copy of his first: a postage-stamp free-kick perfectly placed against Ipswich at Cobham. Greenwood equalised in the first leg of our UEFA Youth League second round tie with a powerful 18-yard strike that flew into the net after he had cut inside and created space for a shot. A brilliant recovery and pass from Romeo Lavia freed Rogers, who needed no second invitation to drive at the Man United backline. news.title: Vote for your Men's Goal of the Month!
Cole Palmer and the four other fastest Blues to 50 Premier League goals
news.body_en: The penalty Cole Palmer converted against Manchester United was his 50th Premier League goal for Chelsea. It is a landmark the Blues' No.10 has quickly reached. The 24-year-old is the third-quickest player in Blues history to reach a half-century of goals in the Premier League era. Palmer has needed just 105 games to do it, with his spot-kick on Saturday his third league goal of the campaign. We list below our top five fastest players to 50 Premier League goals, with Palmer in esteemed company among some of the best attackers in our history. Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink hit the ground running at Stamford Bridge after arriving from Atletico Madrid for a club-record fee. The Dutch striker brought up his 50th Premier League goal in just 84 Blues appearances, with 23 alone in his debut season when he won the Golden Boot award. Diego Costa was the focal point of two Premier League title wins, in 2015 and 2017. The Spanish international reached the 50-goal mark for us in 85 matches, midway through his third and final campaign as a Blue, when he again finished as our top scorer. Palmer’s ratio of almost a goal every other game in the Premier League for the Blues is a phenomenal achievement considering – unlike the other players in this list – he is not a striker. An amazing 22 goals in his maiden campaign set the tone for what was to come. Always a player for the big occasion, Didier Drogba's legendary Chelsea career included 104 Premier League goals, the first 50 of which came in 106 appearances. His goals helped fire us to the Premier League title in 2005, 2006, 2010 and 2015. Signed from Bolton Wanderers in 2000, Eidur Gudjohnsen quickly became a fan favourite with his intelligence, silky touch, and knack for spectacular goals. The Icelandic forward completed the half-century in 153 Premier League outings, playing a crucial role in our back-to-back title successes in the mid-2000s.

news.title: Seven standout stats from Chelsea's win over Manchester United
news.body_en: A dominant second-half performance from the Blues secured a 2-0 victory over Manchester United on Saturday and returned us to the Premier League's top four. And here are seven standout statistics from our win at Stamford Bridge. Cole Palmer scored his 50th Premier League goal for Chelsea on his 105th appearance. He's the third-fastest to reach that milestone for the Blues, after Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink (84 games) and Diego Costa (85 games). The Blues have netted nine goals in the opening five minutes of either half in the Premier League this season. No other team has scored more than three, while only in 2008/09 (10) and 2024/25 (11) have the Blues netted more such goals. Morgan Rogers became the first Chelsea player and just the second Premier League player to reach 10 goal involvements in all competitions this season (six goals, four assists), after Erling Haaland. Rogers’ five league goals make him our top scorer in the competition. Romeo Lavia won possession 14 times against Manchester United, the most by a Chelsea player in a Premier League game since Lewis Hall did so at Fulham in January 2023. It is also the joint-most by any player in the top flight this season, alongside Ipswich Town’s Argentine international midfielder Exequiel Palacios against Nottingham Forest. The Blues have kept two clean sheets in our last three Premier League games, one more than in our previous 28 matches in the competition. They were also Mike Penders’ first Premier League clean sheets, having played the last 15 minutes at Everton and the full 90 minutes against Manchester United, both 2-0 wins. Chelsea won a Premier League home game without conceding for the first time in 13 matches, since a 2-0 victory against Brentford in January. On Saturday, at 23 years and 89 days, we named our joint-second-youngest starting XI in a Premier League match, matching the age of the line-up that faced Newcastle United in October 2024. The 23 years and 21 days of the team that beat Crystal Palace 2-1 in December 2023 remains our youngest of all time in the Premier League.

news.title: Analysis: Midfield engine and fluid forward line too much for Man United
news.body_en: The Blues returned to the Premier League’s top four after overcoming Manchester United at Stamford Bridge. We dive into the post-match statistics to detail how Romeo Lavia’s starring role and our rotating attackers left our opponents beaten. After an evenly balanced first half, the Blues came flying out of the blocks in the second period - not for the first time this season - and Morgan Rogers broke the deadlock with his fifth Premier League goal of the season, making him our top scorer in the competition and the first Chelsea player to reach 10 goal involvements across all competitions. And after Manchester United were reduced to 10 men following a second booking for Lisandro Martinez for a foul on Wesley Fofana, and Cole Palmer swept in the resulting penalty for his 50th Premier League goal for the club, we were able to finish the job in relative comfort with a dominant second-half display. Lavia was voted Player of the Match by supporters on the Chelsea Official App – and it is not hard to see why. The Belgian dominated the midfield on Saturday, covering ground and stepping in with perfect timing to snuff out opposition attacks before they could gain momentum and producing counter-attacking opportunities. The clearest example of that came shortly after half-time, when he created the chance for Rogers to open the scoring. As Bryan Mbeumo tried to shield the ball in the centre-circle, Lavia overpowered him and then reacted quickly to beat Carlos Baleba to the second ball and direct it into Rogers’ feet. The midfielder was also unlucky not to get a second assist when he demonstrated his excellent reading of the game, racing out of nowhere to anticipate a Bruno Fernandes first-time pass and intercept, before sending Palmer running against the United backline. It turned defence into attack in an instant and ended with Estevao Willian firing into the roof of the net, although the goal would be chalked off for the narrowest of VAR offside calls. The Belgian’s five tackles were the most of any player on the pitch and he came away with the ball from four of them. Overall, he regained possession 14 times, not only the highest number in this match, but the most by any Chelsea player in a single fixture for over three-and-a-half years. It's also telling that 12 of those 14 recoveries came in the opposition half and two of them in the Man Utd penalty area. Lavia didn't just sit back and protect our defence; he actively hunted the ball down to win it back from positions that we could threaten our opponents with a quick turnover. Of course, taking advantage of transitions instigated by ball-winners such as Lavia is easier when you have attacking players who can ruthlessly punish opponents. Although Rogers was not far off the halfway line when he received the ball, the way he advanced with purpose towards the hesitant defenders made the goal seem almost inevitable. It was a team effort from our forward line against Manchester United, though. Pedro Neto took on the central striker’s role in Joao Pedro’s absence and did so selflessly, holding up the ball and using his movement to create space for Rogers and Estevao to exploit coming into the channels from wide, while Palmer pulled the strings between the lines. The effect was devastating, as our attack has been so often this season under Xabi Alonso. In total, the Blues managed 19 shots against Man Utd, our highest in a single Premier League match this season. Estevao led the way by providing six of those, also the joint-highest by a Chelsea player in the league this season, in addition to his two goals disallowed. Estevao, Palmer and Rogers all tied for the most chances created in the game, with three each, and also made up the leading three for passes completed in the final third. It was Palmer who topped that particular statistic, completing an impressive 19 of 25 passes in the final third, both game-high numbers. Saturday's match underlined how much Palmer and Rogers love playing against Man Utd. The ex-Manchester City academy duo both have excellent records against their old local rivals: Palmer with five goals in eight games, Rogers with three goals in five games. Further back, Josh Acheampong again showed how he has adapted to life in the Premier League this season. The Academy graduate has been a regular in Alonso’s team, featuring in all but one of our nine league games so far, and continues to produce performances that defy his age and experience. With the movement of our attackers pulling the Man Utd defenders narrow, Acheampong was able to dominate the right flank. He kept Matheus Cunha largely in check while galloping forward to add width to our attacks at the other end. Defensively, only Lavia bettered the 20-year-old’s three successful tackles and 10 ball recoveries, while in possession only Fofana had more than his 90 touches of the ball. In addition, Acheampong’s 12 completed passes in the final third were only behind the attacking trio of Estevao, Palmer and Rogers, and more than any United player apart from Bruno Fernandes. A true all-round performance from our young right-back.

news.title: Analysis: How Chelsea Women saw off Charlton with quick-fire attack
news.body_en: When Chelsea made the trip across London to face Charlton Athletic on Sunday, we faced a side with completely different objectives to our own. The Addicks finished third in the Women's Super League 2 last season and earned promotion to the top flight by winning a play-out against relegated Women's Super League side Leicester City as part of the league's objective to increase the WSL to 14 teams. It's been tough for Charlton so far, and they came into Sunday's match without a single point earned in seven matches this season. From a Chelsea perspective, that meant it was imperative to win, especially with us sitting neck-and-neck with Manchester City at the top of the table. Blues head coach Sonia Bompastor has an oft-used phrase when she says she likes her team to score early to 'kill off the opposition's hope'. That's exactly what we did when Nathalie Bjorn netted after three minutes, then a brace from Melvine Malard and a strike by Ellie Carpenter all came before the 20-minute mark. For a newly-promoted team with no points on the board, against an experienced Chelsea side, that was effectively game over, and second-half goals from Aggie Beever-Jones and Giulia Dragoni completed the 6-0 win. Here's a look at how a ruthless approach secured the three points... There was no holding back on Sunday, as the Blues attempted 36 shots against Charlton, our highest total in a single match in the WSL this season. Our assault on the opposition's back line made sure there was no chance for them to dig in and attempt to frustrate us with a low block, and it also allowed us to build our goal difference to plus 23, with the title race looking like it might come down to fine margins this season. Bompastor's earlier call for the team to be more clinical has been answered, as we have scored in all eight of our WSL fixtures this season. No other team has done so. Malard and Chelsea have been the perfect fit since the striker's summer move from Manchester United. The Blues No9 has already equalled her WSL tally of six managed with the Red Devils last season and is thriving up front in her new home. One of the reasons for her superb form could be that she is focusing solely on finding the back of the net. Against Charlton, she netted her brace in the space of just 10 minutes, making a game-changing contribution early on in the match. If a striker scores twice in a game, they need not contribute much else. In a show of attacking efficiency during her 50 minutes of action, Malard touched the ball 13 times, completing all five of her passes and scoring twice from three shots on goal. It is that deadly form that will strike fear into opposition defences in the weeks to come. Another summer signing who has fit like a glove is Katie McCabe. Her high standards ensure that she puts in consistently strong performances every week and she once again stood out during the win over Charlton. Creating more chances (five) than any other player on the pitch, McCabe also ranked second for crosses attempted (six), completed passes (78) and completed passes in the final third (22). Both McCabe and her right-sided counterpart Carpenter were aggressive in winning the ball back, with the Australian ranking highest for recoveries (12) and the Republic of Ireland captain following just behind her with 11. It was another unselfish performance from McCabe and her performances could well continue to improve as the weeks go by at her new club. Chelsea supporters will have been delighted to see Nathalie Bjorn lead the team out as captain at The Valley following her injury-hit season last term. The experienced defender made her first start of the campaign against Charlton and began the match in the best way possible with her early goal. It was an assured display from Bjorn as she played just over an hour in the back line before being replaced by Alyssa Thompson. Having the Sweden international back in form will be a huge boost as the fixtures continue to come thick and fast in the coming weeks.

news.title: Ellie Carpenter feeling good and taking positives from Charlton win
news.body_en: With her fifth goal of the season in our 6-0 victory over Charlton Athletic at the weekend, Ellie Carpenter has already exceeded last season’s total of three. And it’s only November. The wing-back, now in her second campaign with the Blues, has played a key role in the team’s success this season, starting in all but one of our 13 matches so far. Last week, Carpenter came on at half-time against Roma in the Women’s Champions League with the scores locked at 0-0, scoring within six minutes of the restart. After the match, Sonia Bompastor explained there was some debate over whether or not her introduction was an attack-minded substitution. ‘It's funny, because I had a conversation with the technical staff,' said the head coach following the win over the Italian side. 'I made the final decision, and someone in my technical staff said: "But we need to score, and you are bringing on a defensive player"! ‘We laughed after the game because I said: "Right now she's scoring a lot of goals, so I don't know if she's more defensive or an attacking player”! It worked, so it's good. I was confident Ellie would create a lot in the second half.’ At the moment, Carpenter is covering enough ground down the right flank to be both. She scored against Charlton, but also won the most tackles (three) and made the most ball recoveries (12) of any player on the team. ‘I’m proud of the group,’ the Blues No2 said after the win at The Valley. ‘Our number one goal in this game was to get the three points and keep a clean sheet. We wanted to score, and it’s great to come and see so many different goal scorers. There are a lot of positives from Sunday that we’ll take into the next game.’ A deeper look into Carpenter’s stats shows her impact on the team this season. In the Women's Super League, the Australian has played the most minutes of any outfield Chelsea player (714), is ranked highest for big chances created (seven), has the most touches in the opposition box (56), possession won (46 times) and possession won in the final third (10). She is also second in the team for expected assists (2.79) and chances created (19). Her numbers are not only high within the Chelsea side, but also league-wide. Only Khadija Shaw and Lauren Hemp of Manchester City plus Victoria Pelova of Tottenham Hotspur have had more touches in the opposition box than Carpenter’s 56. Only Hemp has created more chances than Carpenter in the WSL. ‘It feels really good,’ the wing-back continued after the win over Charlton. 'I'm just trying to do my best on the ball in every game, so I'm really proud of that.’

news.title: Sonia Bompastor on why every tiny detail matters for Chelsea this season
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor outlined her high standards at both ends of the pitch after her side recorded a 6-0 victory over Charlton Athletic at The Valley on Sunday afternoon. The Blues fired 36 shots on goal during the 90 minutes, 11 of which were on target, while we also reduced the home side to just six shots in total, with only one of theirs finding the target. We also hit the woodwork twice and held 71 per cent of the possession in a display of total dominance on Sunday afternoon. The six-goal victory returned Chelsea to the top of the Women's Super League standings, level on points with Manchester City. It is our record at both ends of the pitch which separates us from our rivals. The Blues have scored 27 times and conceded just four goals in the WSL, recording a goal difference of +23, which works out as 11 more than our rivals, who are currently on +12. For that very reason, Bompastor stressed the importance of maintaining our attacking ruthlessness throughout the campaign. 'This league is so competitive,' she said. 'Every detail is important. Right now, we are top of the table only on goal difference. We need to make sure we go into every game with the desire to score as many goals as we can as well as the desire not to concede. That's part of our mindset and mentality.' The Chelsea head coach was also delighted with the approach shown by her players from the opening whistle. 'We wanted to start the game strong in terms of the performance, the intensity, being aggressive, but also with the ball,' she explained. 'We wanted to score early in the game and make sure we were going into half-time with the advantage. I think that's what the players have done on the pitch and I'm really pleased about that.' The Blues now have five days to prepare for Saturday's WSL clash against Everton at Stamford Bridge, before a pivotal week with an away Women's Champions League fixture against Hacken on Tuesday 10 November and a blockbuster clash with Man City back at the Bridge on Saturday 14 November.

news.title: Chelsea Diary: Blues prepare for Sunderland trip and Everton showdown
news.body_en: It's another busy week at Chelsea, with Premier League and Women's Super League action to look forward to, a London derby for our young Blues and plenty of exclusive content coming your way on the Chelsea Official App and website. We continue our reflections on the weekend, including the Blues' 2-0 win over Manchester United in the Premier League and CFCW's impressive 6-0 triumph at Charlton Athletic in the Women's Super League. There is reaction, highlights and analysis on the Chelsea Official App and website as we reflect on the latest victories from our sides. Attention will then turn to another important weekend of domestic football, with the Blues preparing for trips to Sunderland and Tottenham Hotspur, while our women's team get ready to welcome Everton to Stamford Bridge. We will hear from Giulia Dragoni on Tuesday, with the Italian midfielder discussing her experiences of adapting to life in England following a summer switch from Roma. Dragoni, who netted against Charlton, will reflect on settling into new surroundings, getting to know her team-mates and adjusting to the demands of English football. There will also be the latest news from Cobham as our men's team continue their preparations for Sunday's Premier League trip to Sunderland. The decisive match of Cobham Next Gen’s opening UEFA Youth League tie arrives on Wednesday afternoon, when the Blues host Flora Tallinn at Cobham in a 1pm kick-off. Following a 2-2 draw away in Estonia last week, there is still all to play for in the second leg, and CFC+ subscribers can watch it live in our Cobham Next Gen vs Flora Tallinn Match Centre. We will also continue building towards the weekend's fixtures on Wednesday, with the latest from Cobham as Alonso and his players prepare for the challenge awaiting them at the Stadium of Light.
